stem: The local council claims that the average number of accidents per year on a particular road is 0.8. Jane claims that the true average is greater than 0.8. She looks at the records for a random sample of 3 recent years and finds that the total number of accidents during those 3 years was 5.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Assume that the number of accidents per year follows a Poisson distribution.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: State null and alternative hypotheses for a test of Jane’s claim.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Test at the 5% significance level whether Jane’s claim is justified.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Jane finds that the number of accidents per year has been gradually increasing over recent years.

State how this might affect the validity of the test carried out in part **(a)(ii)**.
